Run a capture to populate. Findings are recorded the way the Athlink movement screen records them, as a side rather than a number.

What this HUD does not do Joint angles are shown as live measurements from the camera. They are not scored against a safe or unsafe cut off, because no such threshold exists in this app's reference files. The HUD does not detect pain, effort or injury, and it does not diagnose. Anything that matters goes to a pediatrician or physical therapist.

Eleven tests. Each records a side or a yes and no, never a score out of ten. Leaving a field as null is a real answer, not a gap, and it is the correct one whenever the camera or the parent genuinely could not judge it.

Did anything hurt during the screen? The screen records how movements look, not whether they hurt. If any test hurt, log it in the pain check on the Workouts tab. Pain at 3 or more out of 10 pauses the recovery routines until it settles.

Why there are no risk percentages here These are the regions that take load during a growth spurt, listed so you know what to mention at the next visit. Provectus carries no sourced figure for how likely any of them is, so it shows none. Naming a condition and putting a percentage on it would be a diagnosis, and that is a clinician's call.

Growth rate

This is measured growth between your own logged entries. It is the one number on this screen that is not an estimate, so it is worth measuring at the same time of day each time.

About

Provectus is Athlink v2. It is a screening and education tool for athletes aged 5 to 18 and their parents. It does not diagnose, it does not clear anyone to play, and it does not give individual medical or nutrition advice. Numbers shown come from named published methods with their error stated, or they are not shown at all.
